decisions.title: Primary cross-channel type system
decisions.recommendation: Use tuned Inter as the primary UI, body and reading family. Use Geist for display titles. Use Instrument Serif only when an editorial context requires it. Restrict IBM Plex Mono to code, provenance and technical metadata. Revise mobile typography around the Geist and Inter split.
decisions.rationale: A dedicated role-system calibration separated display, reading, serif, mono and mobile decisions. Olli selected Geist for titles, tuned Inter for body, and approved the recommended remaining policies.
decisions.approvalEvidence: User selected Geist for titles and tuned Inter for body, then explicitly approved the recommended primary, serif, mono and mobile policies in the active Codex task.

decisions.title: Gradient-disc role in the identity
decisions.recommendation: Keep the current disc where required, but test whether it becomes a supporting device within a broader identity grammar.

decisions.title: Button and action-control system
decisions.recommendation: Use a 12px moderate radius, solid primary with outlined secondary and text tertiary, one-pixel hover lift, 48px default height, selective directional icons, white primary with light outlined secondary on dark sections, and a full-width primary with text secondary on mobile.
decisions.scope: buttons and action controls across marketing, commerce and responsive contexts
decisions.rationale: A dedicated seven-decision calibration tested shape, hierarchy, depth, scale, icon policy, dark surfaces and mobile behaviour across real action contexts. Olli approved all seven recommended behaviours without edits.
decisions.approvalEvidence: User supplied a complete review export approving all seven recommended control behaviours in the active Codex task.

decisions.title: Product-family and commerce behaviour
decisions.recommendation: Use the homepage five-product roster in research, an aligned catalogue chassis, gradient and copy for product territory, static cores only in repeated family contexts, equal catalogue weight, AI OS first with bundles later, and a vertical mobile catalogue with a persistent purchase summary.
decisions.scope: product-family presentation and commerce sequence across homepage, catalogue, bundle scenarios and mobile
decisions.rationale: The contextual plate tested seven product-family and commerce behaviours. Olli approved the homepage five, aligned catalogue, gradient-and-copy territories, static cores only, equal family weight, live-first commerce and a vertical mobile catalogue with sticky purchase summary. Olli explicitly stated that the general design still needs a lot of work, so this decision approves behaviour only and withholds approval from the plate's visual execution.
decisions.approvalEvidence: User supplied a complete seven-decision export and explicitly withheld approval of the general visual design in the active Codex task.

decisions.title: Centred living product-family homepage direction
decisions.recommendation: Use the centred Hero 03 direction with approved message hierarchy, five equal-size stacked product cards, one coherent product-family read and the Living Core animation system. Preserve the desktop direction while revising the mobile card composition. Pause broader homepage construction until the Living Core gradient system and its cross-channel expression rules are locked.
decisions.scope: homepage opening, message hierarchy, product-family hero composition and Living Core direction
decisions.rationale: Olli approved five of six Hero 03 decisions and described the direction as materially better. Mobile remains an explicit edit. Card, disc, sphere, Wings and static-versus-animated rules require a dedicated component and Living Core system before the homepage continues.
decisions.approvalEvidence: User supplied a complete Hero 03 review approving overall direction, message hierarchy, card stack, animation and product-family read, with mobile marked edit, then explicitly paused the homepage to systemise gradients.

decisions.title: First reference and anti-reference panel
decisions.recommendation: Study Notion, Linear, Stripe, ElevenLabs, and Ramp at deep depth before comparative synthesis.
decisions.scope: Phase 2 research priorities and source selection
decisions.rationale: Olli selected a narrower software-centred panel to favour depth, speed, and direct relevance. Lost cross-category, mature-system, and anti-reference coverage is recorded as a limitation.
decisions.approvalEvidence: User selected Notion, Linear, Stripe, ElevenLabs, and Ramp for deep study in the active Codex task.

decisions.title: The living core: sanctioned continuous motion on product cores
decisions.recommendation: Carve a single named exception into 16-motion.md: the product core may animate continuously when rendered as a living core. Everything else in the motion law is unchanged.
decisions.scope: motion law, gradient treatments, product cores
decisions.rationale: The Living Core is product identity in motion and requires one tightly scoped exception to the otherwise static motion law. The exception preserves a static foreground, exact fallback and one focal animated core rather than granting general animation permission.
decisions.supersedes: The 'gradients never animate' and 'discs never move' clauses of 16-motion.md, for the living-core treatment only.
decisions.approvalEvidence: User explicitly stated 'DEC-MOTION-002 approved' in the active Codex task.

decisions.title: Complete source-gradient library and Living Core expression family
decisions.recommendation: Use the 43 supplied PNG IDs as source evidence, expose 33 unique active cores, preserve ten duplicate IDs as compatibility aliases, accept MZ-G01 as supplied, and use one shared Living Core renderer across disc, sphere, rounded card, pill and Wings expressions.
decisions.scope: source-gradient library, aliases, animation and cross-shape expression family
decisions.rationale: The complete source-PNG library was rebuilt deterministically and reviewed across representative static and animated expressions. The selection does not approve product assignments.
decisions.approvalEvidence: Olli explicitly approved all supplied colours, Living Core animation, current expression categories, MZ-G01 and the duplicate-removal policy in the active Codex task.

decisions.title: Deep Mineral Living Core finish
decisions.recommendation: Use the Deep Mineral finish as the approved research-system default: full opacity, 0.97 exposure, 1.12 saturation, 1.13 contrast, -0.01 lift, 0.76 shade strength, 0.9 bloom strength and 1.1 grain strength.
decisions.scope: Living Core runtime finish only; source PNGs, static twins and product assignments remain unchanged
decisions.rationale: Deep Mineral provides denser colour, firmer blacks, stronger sphere depth and the least-whitewashed finish while preserving exact static authority.
decisions.approvalEvidence: Olli explicitly selected Deep Mineral No. 5 and described its dense colour, firmer blacks and stronger sphere depth as way better in the active Codex task.

decisions.title: Migrate the canonical control plane before completing the full system
decisions.recommendation: Close only the product architecture, identity kernel and minimum canonical-engine requirements before cutover. Transfer remaining strategy, foundations, components, golden outputs, Figma and channels as governed backlog to the new canonical repository.
decisions.scope: repository sequencing, authority transfer and pre-cutover definition of done
decisions.rationale: Continuing large foundation and experience builds inside Mezcorp would deepen the dual-authority problem. The target workbench is now recoverable and can become canonical once the identity kernel and cutover controls pass.
decisions.approvalEvidence: Olli made migration the primary goal, requested immediate recovery protection and ledger reconciliation, and asked that the programme decide what must close before transfer in the active Codex task.

decisions.title: Literal five-product architecture and Living Core assignments
decisions.recommendation: Use literal public product names only and migrate the five stable product IDs with these assignments: AI OS to MZ-G13, Context Engine to MZ-G12, AI Ads System to MZ-G06, Claude Code OS to MZ-G15, and Organic Content OS to MZ-G20.
decisions.scope: public product architecture, stable product IDs and product-to-gradient assignments
decisions.rationale: A literal naming system is clearer and more transferable than an alternate historical-name layer. Olli selected MZ-G12 for Context Engine, moved MZ-G06 to AI Ads System, moved MZ-G20 to Organic Content OS, retained AI OS on MZ-G13 and retained Claude Code OS on MZ-G15.
decisions.approvalEvidence: Olli explicitly removed the Aurora, Forge and Prism naming layer, selected MZ-G12 for Context Engine, assigned MZ-G06 to AI Ads System, assigned MZ-G20 to Organic Content OS, and retained AI OS and Claude Code OS assignments in the active Codex task.
